---

About Us

The Gilchrist Collection is home to 12 stunning wedding venues across the UK, supported by our Head Office team.

We're an ambitious, growing business and believe AI, automation and modern technology have the potential to fundamentally improve how we work.

We're now looking for an AI & Automation Specialist to help us turn that potential into reality.

This is not a role about simply introducing the latest AI tools or encouraging people to use ChatGPT. We're looking for someone who can understand how our business operates, identify genuine opportunities for improvement and then build and implement practical solutions that make a measurable difference.

The Role

This is a newly created role with a broad remit across the entire Gilchrist Collection.

Working closely with the CEO and Chief of Staff, you'll explore how AI, automation and technology can be used positively across both Head Office and our venues to improve efficiency, reduce repetitive work, connect systems, improve decision-making and create better ways of working.

You'll spend time understanding how different parts of the company operate – from sales, marketing and customer enquiries through to operations, finance, HR, administration, reporting and venue management.

You'll identify processes that are unnecessarily manual, repetitive or inefficient and ask: "Is there a better way of doing this?"

Most importantly, you'll then be able to do something about it.

Depending on the problem, that could mean implementing an existing AI platform, creating an automated workflow, connecting different systems through APIs, building an AI agent, developing an internal application or creating a completely new software solution.

We're looking for someone who combines technical ability with commercial thinking. You need to be as comfortable sitting with a department head to understand a business problem as you are getting hands-on and building the solution.

What You'll Do

Work directly with the CEO and Chief of Staff to develop and implement practical uses of AI and automation across The Gilchrist Collection.

Review processes across the entire business, including Head Office and our 12 wedding venues.

Identify repetitive, manual and inefficient processes that could be improved through AI, automation or better technology.

Prioritise opportunities based on their potential business impact, efficiency gains and practicality.

Design, build, test and implement AI-powered tools and automated workflows.

Build internal software, applications and tools where an off-the-shelf solution doesn't meet the business need.

Create AI agents and assistants capable of supporting specific business processes and teams.

Connect existing systems using APIs, webhooks and integrations to reduce manual data entry and duplication.

Develop automated workflows using platforms such as n8n, Make, Zapier or Microsoft Power Automate.

Work with leading AI platforms and models, including tools from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft and others, selecting technology based on the problem rather than being tied to one platform.

Use coding and scripting where appropriate, including technologies such as Python and JavaScript, to create more sophisticated solutions.

Work with databases, APIs and other data sources to enable systems to communicate and information to flow effectively.

Build internal dashboards, reporting tools and applications that give teams better access to information.

Explore opportunities to use AI to improve areas such as customer service, sales, marketing, operations, finance, HR, reporting and administration.

Prototype ideas quickly, test them with users and develop successful concepts into reliable business tools.

Assess new AI technologies and platforms as they emerge and determine whether they have a genuine application within the business.

Improve and maintain solutions after launch rather than treating implementation as the end of the project.

Help colleagues understand how to use AI effectively, responsibly and securely.

Establish sensible standards around AI use, data handling, security and access.

Measure the impact of implemented solutions, including time saved, costs reduced, improved productivity and other measurable business benefits.

What We're Looking For

We're looking for a builder and problem-solver.

You don't necessarily need to come from a particular industry, but you do need to be able to demonstrate that you've used AI, automation and technology to solve genuine business problems.

You'll ideally have:

Hands-on experience implementing AI-powered solutions within a real business environment.

Strong knowledge of current generative AI platforms and large language models.

Experience building AI applications, assistants, agents or automated workflows.

Experience with automation platforms such as n8n, Make, Zapier, Power Automate or similar.

The ability to code and build practical software solutions, ideally using Python, JavaScript or similar technologies.

Experience working with APIs, webhooks, databases and system integrations.

An understanding of how modern AI APIs and models can be incorporated into applications and business processes.

Experience building internal tools, applications, dashboards or other business systems.

The ability to rapidly prototype ideas and turn successful prototypes into robust, usable solutions.

A strong understanding of data security, permissions, privacy and the risks associated with introducing AI into business processes.

Commercial awareness – you'll understand that the best technical solution isn't necessarily the most complicated one.

The ability to understand a business process, identify the real problem and determine whether AI, automation, conventional software or a process change is the right answer.

Strong communication skills and the confidence to work with people who have very different levels of technical knowledge.

A proactive mindset. We don't want to provide you with a list of projects and simply ask you to build them; we want you to find opportunities we haven't identified yet.

Genuine curiosity about AI and emerging technology, combined with the judgement to separate useful innovation from hype.

What We're Not Looking For

This role probably isn't right for someone whose AI experience is primarily using ChatGPT, Copilot or other AI tools as an end user.

Equally, we're not looking for a purely theoretical AI researcher.

We want someone who has built things.

That could include automations, AI agents, internal applications, system integrations, reporting tools or bespoke software.

When you apply, we'd particularly like to hear about the problems you've solved, what you built, the technology you used and – most importantly – what difference it made.

Why Join Us?

This is an unusual opportunity to join a business at a point where there is significant scope to shape how AI and automation are used.

You won't be joining an established AI department or inheriting a long list of legacy projects.

Instead, you'll have the opportunity to look across the company, identify where technology can make the biggest difference and build solutions from the ground up.

You'll benefit from:

£50,000 salary, depending on experience and track record.

A newly created role with genuine scope to shape how AI is used across the company.

Direct access to and collaboration with the CEO and Chief of Staff.

A remit covering the entire organisation rather than one department.

The freedom to explore and recommend new technologies and approaches.

The opportunity to build internal software, AI tools and automations rather than simply administer existing systems.

A varied working environment spanning Head Office and 12 wedding venues.

The opportunity to see the direct impact of the systems you build.

A business committed to investing in technology where it delivers genuine value.

A full-time, permanent position.

Please note: this is a full-time, office-based role, Monday to Friday.

We believe being embedded in the business is particularly important for this position. You'll need to spend time with teams, understand how they actually work and identify opportunities that aren't always obvious from a process document or Teams call.

Interested?

If you're excited by the potential of AI but even more excited by actually building things with it, we'd love to hear from you.

Please apply with your CV and include examples of AI, automation or software solutions you've personally designed or built.

We're particularly interested in hearing:

What problem were you trying to solve?

What did you build?

Which technologies did you use?

What was your personal involvement in building it?

What measurable impact did it have?

A GitHub profile, portfolio, demonstration, case study or examples of previous projects would also be very welcome.

Pay: From £50,000.00 per year

Benefits:

Company events

Company pension

On-site parking

Work Location: In person

We're hiring a Forward Deployed Engineer to lead the earliest, most open stage of our client work.

This is a forward deployed engineering role that combines hands-on technical ownership with a prominent client relationship, working directly with customer teams to solve their hardest challenges

You'll be the first engineer through the door on a new client engagement. Before there's a team, before there's a plan, with no one ahead of you telling you how to build it.

Just a client trusting you to work out what's possible, then build the proof a delivery team can scale from.

Most engineering roles start once the hard decisions are made. This one starts before them.

If that sounds exciting rather than daunting, this could be for you.

Why you'd want this

You decide how the work gets done.

Most companies wrap their AI accounts in governance and access controls that block half of what's useful. We don't. Swap one AI tool for another, wire them into your stack, whatever suits the problem. No permission needed.

The work spans sectors, from healthcare and commerce to media and education, and it's live transformation that ships.

On a recent 19-week build, an AI insights platform turning complex data into clear, multilingual analysis, AI was embedded from day three and 80.5% of authored commits carried verifiable AI co-authorship.

We call the approach Run: deliver something the business needs now, use that work to set better engineering practices, and leave the team stronger than you found it. You're close to clients from the start, so the effect of your decisions is visible.

About hedgehog lab

We're a UK digital product consultancy and a certified B Corp, with 20 years behind us and teams in Edinburgh, Newcastle, Leeds, Manchester and London.

AI reaches beyond the engineering floor. Around 40 people across the business, recruitment and operations included, are working out how AI changes their own roles.

What you'll do

Turn customer goals into a solution architecture and technology choices

Build proofs of concept that validate your design and hand off cleanly

Define the agentic engineering pipeline: tooling, workflows and guardrails for AI coding agents

Shape the quality strategy, including test approach and code review

Make other engineers more capable, pairing on real work and leaving patterns client teams can own

Own the architectural decision records

Who's this is for

You'll be in front of clients from the first week, not just building behind the scenes. Shaping ambiguous problems and explaining your thinking to non-technical people is core to the job. If you'd rather keep your head down and code, this isn't for you.

Experience you'll need to be considered

Real experience using AI agents to build production software, not copy-pasting from ChatGPT

The ability to break down a complicated, poorly defined problem and ship something that works

Strong TypeScript or Python, comfortable across the full stack, with frameworks such as NestJS or FastAPI

Experience meeting and presenting to clients directly

Strong written communication, especially for ADRs and docs others rely on

Experience in consulting, professional services or a forward-deployed role

A pragmatic take on architecture, sized to POC, pilot or production

Where you'll work

Whilst there's no set number of days you're required to be in the office each week, we really value spending time together in person, both as a team and with our clients.

There will be times when we'll need you to be in one of our offices or at a client site for important meetings, workshops and key moments.

To make that work, you'll need to be based within 50 miles of one of our offices in Edinburgh, Newcastle, Leeds, Manchester or London.

How to apply

Apply below, or get in touch if you want to talk it through first.

About Strathclyde Partnership for Transport

Strathclyde Partnership for Transport (SPT) is the largest of Scotland’s seven Regional Transport Partnerships, serving a population of more than 2.2 million people across 12 local authority areas in the West of Scotland.

SPT’s role is to bring together local authorities and key regional and national partners to plan and deliver an integrated, sustainable transport system that supports inclusive economic growth, tackles inequality, and improves quality of life. At the heart of this is a clear ambition: to deliver a world-class, low-carbon transport system that meets the needs of people and communities now and in the future.

SPT sits at the centre of regional transport planning, combining strategic insight, robust analysis, and practical delivery. The organisation plans and supports transport across all modes, working closely with councils, Transport Scotland, the Scottish Government, operators, and communities to shape how transport services evolve over time.

Alongside its strategic planning role, SPT delivers and supports a wide range of transport activity across the region. This includes investment in bus services, infrastructure and subway, management of major transport programmes, and the delivery of passenger-focused improvements that help keep communities connected.

SPT is now entering a period of significant transformation. Completion of the Subway Modernisation project, major programmes such as Bus Reform and Clyde Metro represent some of the most ambitious transport initiatives ever undertaken in the West of Scotland.

Together, they will reshape how public transport is planned, governed, and delivered, placing passengers, communities and long-term sustainability at the heart of decision-making.

This is an organisation with a strong public service ethos, a collaborative culture and a growing national profile. For professionals who want to work at scale, influence long-term outcomes and help deliver meaningful change, SPT offers a uniquely compelling environment.

You can read more at our SPT website.

About this role:

We are seeking an Artificial Intelligence Lead to join our Digital team on an 18-month fixed-term contract to drive the exploration, implementation and responsible adoption of AI across SPT.

Reporting directly to the Head of Digital Technology, you will lead work to improve SPT’s AI and automation maturity, identifying high-value opportunities that can reduce costs, improve customer experience and increase administrative efficiency. You will drive forward Microsoft Copilot across the Microsoft technology estate, while also assessing other AI platforms, developing proofs of concept and piloting practical solutions including intelligent document management, customer communications, reporting and the automation of repetitive processes.

Working collaboratively with colleagues across Digital, data, information governance and business teams, you will turn organisational challenges into safe, practical AI opportunities and support successful solutions into operational use. You will also build organisational capability through training, workshops and clear communications; contribute to SPT’s AI strategy and acceptable-use standards; maintain oversight of approved AI tools; and ensure our approach remains aligned with data protection requirements, emerging legislation and Scottish Government guidance.

About You

You will have a degree or equivalent experience in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning or a related discipline as well as an in-depth understanding of AI concepts and tools.

We are looking for someone who can identify valuable AI opportunities by engaging stakeholders, assessing and improving organisational maturity and translating business problems into practical solutions. You will bring hands-on experience of developing proofs of concept, prototypes or pilot solutions; implementing AI-driven workflows such as OCR, automation and reporting; and comparing AI platforms and tools. You will also understand data governance, GDPR, emerging AI legislation and relevant UK and Scottish regulatory frameworks. Knowledge of cloud-based AI services, document management systems and customer communication tools would be advantageous.

You will be an analytical and strategic thinker with strong problem-solving skills, able to explain complex concepts clearly to non-technical audiences and deliver engaging training, workshops and written guidance. Collaborative, organised and motivated by innovation, you will be comfortable working across teams, maintaining clear AI documentation and contributing to SPT’s AI strategy. You will be a self-starter with high personal standards who can adapt to change, challenge positively, take ownership of issues and see them through to completion.

Full time hours will be 35 hours per week Monday to Friday. However, you may be required to undertake work outwith this norm to meet the responsibilities of the post.

Whilst you will be based at 131 St Vincent Street, Glasgow, SPT operate a hybrid working pattern which allows 40% home working (i.e. 2 days per week Monday to Friday).

Please note, this position falls into the low-risk category under the Alcohol and Drugs policy and therefore is subject to for-cause testing procedures.

Further details of the role and key responsibilities are set out in the job description.

33 Days Annual and Public Holiday Entitlement then 41 days after 5 years’ service

Based onsite full time in our Leatherhead, Surrey office.

This role will sit within our Technology team and requires an individual with a high-level of competency in data analytics, automation and AI and a proactive approach to problem solving and the confidence to independently learn new technologies. This is a junior role within the team and would suit a recent graduate in Computer Science or similar.

ESP is a business dedicated to continuous improvement and the introduction of this role aligns with our strategy to sustain our leading position within the market. To do this, we need the people, systems and processes in place that enable us to offer an ease of business that secures customer loyalty. This role will be dedicated to identifying opportunities and improvements to enhance our current systems and their ability both through the use data analytics and artificial intelligence (AI) solutions to identify opportunities, realise efficiency savings, minimise risks and improve customer service. You need to be passionate about making a difference and inspiring technological advancements that make a real impact.

Key Accountabilities

- The Data & AI Engineer is accountable for using software, artificial intelligence and machine learning to analyse and interpret large amounts of data and support the successful implementation of new technologies and improved system functionality, including automation across ESP.
- Review and understand business processes and data requirements and specify data analytics and automation solutions
- Produce simple to understand management insight using Microsoft Fabric, Power BI and machine learning to analyse large amounts of data to support improved decision making,
- Implement process automation solutions using Microsoft Copilot Studio, Power platform (and other AI solutions and relevant scripting languages) to help the business to improve business efficiency and customer experience
- Maintain and support data platform to ensure data security, integrity and accuracy in all reports and analytics.
- Maintain and support automation solutions to ensure continued efficient operation, and business process continuity.
- Continuously improve and optimise existing reports and automation processes.

They will be an advocate for Data Analytics and AI within the business and will take a proactive role in ensuring that individuals and teams have the systems and resources in place that will enable ESP to deliver in line with our fast-paced and agile commercial strategy. They must demonstrate effective communication skills with multiple stakeholders at all levels of the business, and ensure there is transparency of project progress, risks, and successes.

This individual will produce simple to understand management insight by using technologies including artificial intelligence (AI), to analyse large amounts of data to help improve decision making.

They will take responsibility for identifying the training they require to understand and implement technology that supports the delivery of objectives defined for business change projects. They will remain aware of new technologies and capabilities that may be of benefit to ESP and will provide recommendations for continuous improvement opportunities

Key Responsibilities

- Analyse and interpret large amounts of data from a range of sources – using technical, analytical and communication skills to collect and examine data to help provide management insight to make better informed decisions and solve problems.

- Advanced knowledge of relevant scripting languages (e.g.Python, R, SQL, Java Script

Title: AI Engineer
Description:
Practice Group / Department:
Legal Innovation, Design & Technology - London

Job Description

Norton Rose Fulbright is a global law firm with more than 3,000 lawyers advising clients across locations in the United States, Europe, Canada, Latin America, Asia, Australia, Africa and the Middle East. We provide a full scope of legal services to the world’s preeminent corporations and financial institutions.

Our vision is to be a world class business, profitable, ambitious, cooperative and considerate, supporting our clients and people through our global business principles of Quality, Unity and Integrity.

With over 7,000 employees worldwide, our culture is the thread that connects us. Our strategy and culture are closed connected – defined by shared ambition, global collaboration and a one-team mindset. We believe pioneering work happens when people are empowered to think beyond boundaries, explore new opportunities and grow through diverse experiences. Alongside the right skills and experience, we are looking for people who are innovative, commercially minded, and motivated by the impact of the work they do – ready to share in our ambition and help shape what comes next.

Because while individuals can do well, together we achieve something extraordinary.

Role Purpose

We are building a new R&D capability focused on developing data-driven and AI-enabled solutions for legal services and the wider business of law.

The AI Engineer will build end-to-end AI capabilities for R&D products: agentic workflows, retrieval and context, agent and evaluation harnesses, and the user-facing features around them. Working with the Head of R&D, you will translate agreed product and technical designs into secure, observable and maintainable products.

This is a hands-on full-stack AI engineering role, with applied AI product delivery at its core. You will build AI workflows, tools and integrations, evaluation and observability capabilities, together with the APIs, services and user interfaces needed to ship them reliably.

This is not a research-only role. You will apply agreed enterprise architecture, security and deployment patterns, while taking practical responsibility for code quality, testing, monitoring and troubleshooting with product, data, technology and security teams.

You will join a small, hands-on multidisciplinary team. Each team member will work collaboratively across discovery, prototyping, engineering, productionisation and continuous improvement.

Key Responsibilities

- Build complete AI-enabled product features across user interface, backend, AI orchestration, retrieval and approved enterprise integrations.

- Design and build agentic AI workflows using structured outputs, tool calling, workflow orchestration, document processing, human-review steps and appropriate controls.

- Build reusable agent harnesses: practical runtime patterns around tools, state, context, approvals, traces and test fixtures that make agents consistent, inspectable and safe to use.

- Build grounded retrieval and context patterns using approved data products, search indexes, document repositories and permission-aware sources; provide evidence and citations where appropriate.

- Design and operate evaluation harnesses for AI workflows, including curated test sets, representative scenarios, automated and human grading, regression tests, trace review and user-feedback loops.

- Manage prompts, model configuration, tool schemas and routing as tested product assets, including fallbacks and cost/latency trade-offs.

- Implement AI observability through traces, logs, metrics and evaluation results, so quality, reliability, failure modes, latency and cost are visible and can be improved.

- Build clear APIs and integrate AI products with approved data, document, search and business systems.

- Build usable interfaces that help users understand AI output, inspect supporting evidence, provide feedback and complete review or approval steps.

- Write maintainable Python and TypeScript code; use Docker, Git, automated testing and CI/CD to make development, testing and deployment repeatable.

- Apply agreed security, authentication, data-handling, deployment and release patterns, working with the relevant firm technology teams where needed

Initial Focus

- End-to-end agentic AI features and reusable harnesses for Radar and other named R&D products.

- A practical evaluation and test capability that lets the team compare prompts, models, tools and retrieval approaches before and after release.

- Grounded AI workflows that combine firm data, documents, market or regulatory information and user context into useful, attributable outputs.

- Interfaces that make AI output, confidence, evidence, controls and next actions clear to lawyers and business users.

What Success Looks Like

- R&D products use AI workflows that are grounded in trusted context, observable in operation and understandable to users.

- AI quality is measured rather than assumed; evaluation results, traces and feedback lead to demonstrable improvements in usefulness, reliability, latency and cost.

- The engineer can independently take a well-scoped AI workflow from problem definition to controlled deployment.

- At least one AI component, harness or evaluation capability is reused by a second R&D product or workflow.

- Promising prototypes have a repeatable path to controlled release, monitoring and improvement.

Essential Skills and Experience

- At least three years’ professional experience delivering production AI products, with demonstrable recent experience building AI-enabled products or workflows in a SaaS environment. Experience in legal technology or a law firm is not required, but would be advantageous.

- Strong Python, plus practical TypeScript or JavaScript. Able to build APIs and services using FastAPI, Flask or comparable technologies, and usable interfaces using React, Next.js or equivalent.

- Demonstrable experience building AI-enabled products or workflows using LLM APIs, structured outputs, retrieval and embeddings, tool calling, agents or workflow orchestration.

- Experience building agentic systems using an agent framework or custom orchestration patterns, including tools, state/context management and human-review or approval controls.

- Experience evaluating AI workflows using representative test sets, scenario design, model or prompt experiments, trace review, user feedback, and automated or human grading.

- Experience taking AI features from prototype into controlled production, including testing, monitoring, troubleshooting and ongoing improvement.

- Experience with AI observability, tracing and evaluation tooling.

- Strong understanding of grounded retrieval, context quality, evidence/citations and the ways in which AI systems fail.

- Experience designing APIs and integrating with enterprise systems; sound handling of authentication, authorisation, secrets and sensitive data.

- Comfort with Docker, Git, automated testing and CI/CD. You do not need to be a dedicated platform engineer, but should be able to ship maintainable, repeatable work.

- Strong debugging and systems-thinking skills, including the ability to diagnose failures across models, prompts, tools, retrieval and integrations.

- Able to explain AI behaviour, evaluation results and technical trade-offs clearly to technical and non-technical colleagues.

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

To attract the best people, we strive to create a diverse and inclusive environment where everyone can bring their whole selves to work, have a sense of belonging, and realize their full career potential.
Our new enabled work model allows our people to have more flexibility in the way they choose to work from both the office and a remote location, while continuing to deliver the highest standards of service.
